title: PDF Too Big to Email? Make a Smaller, Readable Copy
description: Check your email attachment limit, compress a PDF copy and inspect small text before sending. Learn when a sharing link is a better option.
direct: Check the sending account and the recipient's attachment rules first. Compress a separate PDF copy, then verify its file size and readability. If it is still too large, share an access-controlled link or send only the pages the recipient needs.
figureAlt: Three checks for an email PDF: check the receiving limit, inspect text and images in a compressed copy, then test the attachment or sharing link.
figureCaption: File size and legibility both matter. This is an explanatory workflow, not an App screenshot.
cards: Know the limit
Personal Gmail allows 25 MB of attachments in total. Work or school limits can be set by an administrator.
Check the copy
Small text, form fields, signatures and page count matter more than an advertised compression percentage.
Use a link when needed
A link avoids a large email attachment, but introduces hosting permissions and access requirements.
sections: Check the whole message, not just one PDF

Google lists a 25 MB total attachment limit for personal Gmail and says larger attachments are replaced with a Google Drive link. Work and school account limits may be set by an administrator. Microsoft's Outlook help distinguishes account types and notes that message limits can include the attachment and email itself. The recipient can impose a lower limit too. Read the actual rejection message rather than assuming every provider has the same cap.
Compress a copy in the browser

Open our PDF compressor, choose the PDF and start with the Balanced quality option. Compress and download a separate copy. Supported processing runs locally in your browser. Browser PDF exports include a small Just Compress app logo watermark, so check that this is acceptable for your recipient before using it for an application or formal document.
Check the result before attaching it

Open the new PDF and compare the first page, the smallest text, diagrams and any signatures with the original. Check page count and file size. Compression can reduce image quality, and an already optimized PDF may barely shrink. Do not promise a fixed percentage or assume that a successful export preserves every document feature. Keep a signed original and follow any requirements for digitally signed files.
If it is still too large

Send only the pages the recipient needs if that is allowed, or use a sharing link from an approved service. In Gmail, an oversized attachment may be replaced with a Drive link. In Apple Mail, Mail Drop supports attachments up to 5 GB subject to its service limits. These options upload a copy for sharing. Check recipient permissions and any expiry instead of describing them as no-upload delivery.
On iPhone

Our App, PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge, offers PDF compression and related document tools. Check the verified App Store listing below for current purchase options. Export a copy, inspect the actual PDF, then attach it using your mail app. The app name does not establish that every export will satisfy a particular portal or mail server.
steps: Check the account, total attachment size and recipient requirements.
Compress a separate copy. Inspect small text, page count and any marks or signatures.
Attach the checked copy, or share an approved link and verify recipient access.
faqs: What size should I target for email?
Use the actual sending and receiving limits, counting all attachments. Leave room under the applicable limit. There is no universal safe size for every account.
Will PDF compression always make the file much smaller?
No. Image-heavy documents may shrink more than text-heavy or already optimized files. Inspect the actual result and readability.
Does the free browser PDF tool add a watermark?
Yes. Browser PDF exports include a small Just Compress app logo watermark. Check the output and the recipient's requirements before sending.

title: Video Too Big for WhatsApp? Choose the Right Sending Method
description: Choose between a smaller chat video, a document attachment and a Status clip. Check the current limit, compress a copy and verify what your recipient receives.
direct: First decide how you want to send the video. A chat video, a document attachment and a Status update have different rules. Keep the original, check the limit shown in your WhatsApp app, then make a smaller copy only if you need one.
figureAlt: Three separate paths: a chat video for convenient viewing, a document for sharing a file, or a Status clip with a duration limit.
figureCaption: Choose the delivery type before choosing a compression setting. This is a workflow diagram, not a WhatsApp screen.
cards: Chat video
Best for viewing directly in the conversation. WhatsApp may compress media; pre-compression does not guarantee it will leave your file unchanged.
Document
Best when you want to send a file attachment. WhatsApp currently documents a 2 GB document limit. The recipient still needs to download and play the file.
Status
A separate publishing route. Check the duration and options in Status rather than applying document limits.
sections: Which limit applies?

There is no single 16 MB limit for every WhatsApp video workflow. In its current media help, WhatsApp describes default video limits of 100 MB at 720p for faster connections and 64 MB at 480p for slower connections. It separately lists a 2 GB document limit and a 90-second Status duration. These are contextual limits, not a promise that every version or receiving device accepts every file. Check the current app message and the official help linked below.
Make a smaller sharing copy

Start with a short representative clip. Open our browser video compressor, select the video, choose a quality level and compress. Download the result, check its actual size, and watch a bright area, motion and any on-screen text. If it looks too soft, use a less aggressive setting or shorten only material you do not need. The original should remain your editing copy.
On iPhone

Our App, Video Compressor & MP4 Convert, supports video compression and conversion. Its current App Store listing is linked below for features, device requirements and purchase options. Export a copy, inspect it in Files or Photos, then attach that result in WhatsApp. This page does not claim a particular export will pass every receiving limit.
Still cannot send it?

Read the exact error. A file can be small enough but still have a format, playback or connection problem. Try playing the exported copy locally and test one short clip with the recipient. If you are sharing a document, use the attachment control and choose the document or file option available in your version. A full-size file uses the recipient's storage and data too.
Keep privacy and color separate

Our browser compressor processes the supported clip locally; sending it through WhatsApp is a separate action. If colors change after sharing, compare the original and received copy before treating the problem as file size. The HDR and HEVC guides below explain those different checks.
steps: Choose chat video, document or Status. Read the current limit for that route.
Keep the original. Make one smaller copy and inspect the actual size and playback.
Send a test to the intended destination. Check what the recipient actually receives.
faqs: Does making the video smaller prevent WhatsApp compression?
No. WhatsApp can still process a media attachment. Pre-compression helps control the input size; it does not guarantee an unchanged delivered video.
Is every WhatsApp video limited to 16 MB?
No. Delivery type and current app behavior matter. The current official media help distinguishes connection-dependent media limits, a 2 GB document limit and a separate Status duration.
Why does a small video still fail?
Size is only one check. Inspect the error, accepted format, playback and network connection, then test a short copy.

title: What does no-upload file processing mean?
description: No-upload processing means the selected file operation runs on your device. The webpage still loads software from the internet. Check the file workflow, website analytics and any later sharing step separately.
direct: No-upload processing means the selected file operation runs on your device. The webpage still loads software from the internet. Check the file workflow, website analytics and any later sharing step separately.
figureAlt: Local processing keeps the file operation on the device. Cloud processing uploads a copy to a remote service.
figureCaption: An explanatory data-flow diagram. A website can load software and optional analytics separately from processing your selected file.
cards: Local operation
The selected file is processed on your device.
Website requests
The page and software still need to load. Optional analytics is a separate choice.
Sharing the result
Email, storage and messaging destinations have their own data flows.
sections: Three different data flows

Loading a webpage, processing a document and sharing its output are different actions. A local compressor can keep your PDF on the device while the hosting service receives ordinary connection requests. Optional website analytics can record a page visit after consent without receiving the selected file.
What to check before selecting a file

Read where processing happens, what output the tool creates and which limitations matter for your task. A server deletion promise describes uploaded files; a genuinely local operation avoids that processing upload. A private file still needs a secure device and an appropriate sharing destination.
When local processing is a practical fit

Simple compression, trimming, conversion and basic document edits can often run locally. Very large files may exceed a browser tab's resources. Keep the original, try a representative copy and inspect the result instead of assuming every supported-looking extension will work.
What local processing does not guarantee

It does not promise that a site never loads external resources, that a device is secure, or that sending the result through another service stays local. Our website privacy page explains the separate optional analytics controls.
steps: Identify where the file operation runs.
Keep an original and verify the exported copy.
Check the destination before sending a private file.
faqs: Does no upload mean the website is offline?
No. The page and processing software can load from the internet. A selected file can still be processed locally.
Does downloading the result share it with someone?
Saving a copy and sending it to another person are different steps. The chosen destination determines the sharing behavior.

description: Start with the actual job: a smaller PDF, a shorter recording, a compatible video or a photo layout. Choose a browser tool for a supported one-off task, and inspect its output before moving to a batch workflow.

cards: PDF
Compression and document tasks. Check marks and document features.
Audio
Compression, conversion and editing solve different problems.
Video and photos
Check compatibility and color separately from size.
sections: Documents

Use Compress PDF for a smaller copy, Merge PDF for combining documents, or JPG to PDF for turning selected images into a document. Browser PDF exports include a small app logo watermark. Check readability, signatures, form fields and the recipient's requirements before sending.
Audio

Use the audio compressor for encoded file size, M4A to MP3 for that format conversion, and Trim or Split for removing or dividing sections. These are separate operations. A different extension or a shorter clip does not guarantee a particular receiving app will accept it.
Video and photos

For a short compatible clip, try the browser video compressor or MOV-to-MP4 converter. The HDR checker reads metadata; it does not convert color. Use the photo combiner for one grid or long image. Keep originals and check image quality, orientation, audio and actual file size.
When a native App is a better fit

Repeated batches and larger files may be more practical in an installed App. Our App directory lists the current published versions, full store names, real screenshots and access options. Native Apps have their own purchase terms; a free browser tool does not establish that the App is free.

Inspect the output, then decide whether a native batch workflow helps.
faqs: Which browser tool should I use first?
Choose the operation that matches the problem. The Tools directory links the available browser tasks.
Will every App be free because the website is free?
No. Check each App's current store listing and in-app purchase offer.

title: Browser, native App or cloud tool: how to choose
description: Choose by the operation and data flow. A local browser tool suits a supported quick task. A native App can suit repeated device workflows. A cloud service may help when collaboration or remote processing is required.
direct: Choose by the operation and data flow. A local browser tool suits a supported quick task. A native App can suit repeated device workflows. A cloud service may help when collaboration or remote processing is required.
figureAlt: Local processing keeps the file operation on the device. Cloud processing uploads a copy to a remote service.
figureCaption: An explanatory data-flow diagram. A website can load software and optional analytics separately from processing your selected file.
cards: Browser
Convenient for one supported task. Device resources still matter.
Native App
Useful for focused repeated workflows. Verify features and access.
Cloud service
Useful when the task needs a remote service. Check the upload and sharing rules.
sections: Local browser tool

There is no installation for a quick supported job. The selected file operation can run on your device, but memory, browser support and file complexity limit what is practical. Read the output notes: our browser PDF exports include a small app logo watermark.
Native App

An installed App can provide a focused import, batch, export and sharing workflow. That does not make every feature free or every App offline. Read the current App description and privacy information for the actual product. Our directory distinguishes published versions from unverified availability.
Cloud service

A server workflow can provide remote processing, shared work or team access. The service receives the files it needs for that operation. Check access, retention, deletion, recipient permissions and any organizational requirements before using it.
A useful decision test

Ask whether another service needs the content to complete the job. For a mechanical local operation, a supported local tool may be enough. For collaboration or content analysis, choose an appropriate service and share only what the task requires. Cost depends on the actual offer; this page does not invent competitor prices or savings.
steps: Define the operation and output requirements.
Check local support and the actual data flow.
Use one representative file to compare the result before committing a whole batch.
faqs: Is one approach always the most private?
No. Avoiding an unnecessary processing upload reduces one source of exposure, but device security, access and sharing requirements still matter.
Does a lower price prove a tool is the right choice?
No. Compare the task, data flow, output limitations and current offer.

title: Sign, merge and compress a PDF on iPhone
description: Keep your original documents. Combine only the pages you need, make any visual edits on a copy, and inspect the result before sending. PDF compression can change document features, so digitally signed or fillable files need particular care.
direct: Keep your original documents. Combine only the pages you need, make any visual edits on a copy, and inspect the result before sending. PDF compression can change document features, so digitally signed or fillable files need particular care.
figureAlt: Local processing keeps the file operation on the device. Cloud processing uploads a copy to a remote service.
figureCaption: An explanatory data-flow diagram. A website can load software and optional analytics separately from processing your selected file.
cards: Merge
Confirm page order and include only the required pages.
Sign or mark
Keep visual marks distinct from existing digital signatures.
Compress
Check readability and whether document features survive.
sections: Plan the output before editing

Check the recipient's page order, size limit and signature requirements. A typed or drawn signature is a visible mark; it is not the same as preserving an existing cryptographic digital signature. Follow the requirements for the document you are sending.
Use a separate working copy

Our App, PDF Compressor: Sign & Merge, lists merging, page reordering, drawn or typed signatures, watermarks and compression in its current published version. Use the available document tools on a working copy and keep the originals separate.
Compress only after checking what must be preserved

The current App listing explains that compression may create image-backed PDF pages and remove selectable text, forms, links, annotations, metadata or layers. If those features are required, do not assume a smaller PDF retains them. Keep the original and choose an appropriate output workflow.
Inspect the exported file

Open the exported PDF. Check page order and count, small text, any visible signature, links and fields that the recipient requires. Confirm the actual file size and try the intended upload or mail workflow before deleting a source copy.
steps: Keep the original and define the required output.
Use the available merge and visual-editing tools on a copy.
Inspect any compressed export before sending it.
faqs: Does compression preserve forms and selectable text?
Not necessarily. The current App listing warns that compression can create image-backed pages and remove document features.
Is the browser output identical to the iPhone App output?
No. They are different tools. Our browser PDF exports include a small app logo watermark; inspect the actual output from the tool you use.

title: How to compress an audio file on iPhone
description: Make one smaller sharing copy and listen to it before exporting a full recording. The useful setting depends on duration, codec and content. A format conversion alone does not guarantee a smaller or accepted file.
direct: Make one smaller sharing copy and listen to it before exporting a full recording. The useful setting depends on duration, codec and content. A format conversion alone does not guarantee a smaller or accepted file.
figureAlt: Local processing keeps the file operation on the device. Cloud processing uploads a copy to a remote service.
figureCaption: An explanatory data-flow diagram. A website can load software and optional analytics separately from processing your selected file.
cards: Duration
Longer recordings need more data at the same bitrate.
Codec and bitrate
A file extension does not tell you the quality or exact size.
Listening check
Choose the smallest copy that remains clear enough for your purpose.
sections: Check the receiving requirement

Read the destination's actual size, duration and format limits. Do not assume email, a messaging attachment and a document upload use the same cap. Inspect the error separately from the filename extension.
Use the available audio workflow

Our App, Audio Compressor MP3 Converter, lists compression, conversion, trimming and audio extraction. Its current release accepts one file or a batch for compression and adds silence removal. Import a copy, choose an available setting and export one representative test.
Listen before applying a stronger setting

Check soft speech, consonants, background noise and music at ordinary listening volume. Lossy encoding discards information; raising the bitrate later cannot recover it. If the copy sounds watery or dull, choose a less aggressive setting and compare again.
Measure the exported copy

Check actual size, duration and playback in the receiving app. Keep the best original for future editing. For a short browser-supported recording, the free browser audio tool is an alternative; it uses the device's resources and is a separate product from the native App.
steps: Check the destination and keep an original.
Export one representative section using an available setting.
Listen, inspect the size and test it in the destination.
faqs: Will converting M4A to MP3 always shrink the file?
No. Size depends on the encoded bitrate, duration and other settings. Check the actual exported file.
Is file compression the same as dynamic compression?
No. File compression changes the encoded file size. Dynamic compression changes level differences in the audio.
